title: A toolbox to study metabolic status of Drosophila melanogaster larvae
protocol: Using forceps, collect 20 larvae at the stage of interest in a 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube.
Weigh the collected larvae with a precision scale.
Freeze the larvae on dry ice.
Thaw twenty frozen larvae for 5 minutes on ice.
Add a quality control (QC) sample consisting of a mixture of 5 representative metabolites to the samples.
Perform exactly the same steps with the QC sample as with the larvae samples.
Keep samples and solvents ≤ 4°C during the whole procedure.
Add 240 μL of methanol on ice.
Add 48 μL of deionized water on ice.
Add 200 μL of chloroform on ice.
Homogenize samples with a small teflon pestle for 2 min and resuspend with a pipette, on ice.
Place the samples in liquid nitrogen for 1 min.
Allow samples to thaw on ice for 2 min.
Repeat freezing and thawing steps two more times.
Add 120 μL of deionized water to each sample on ice.
Add 120 μL of chloroform to each sample on ice.
Vortex the samples for 5 s.
Centrifuge the samples at 10,000 g for 15 min at 4°C.
Transfer each phase to a different 1.5 mL Eppendorf tube on ice.
Make a hole with a needle in the caps of the tubes containing the aqueous phase.
Introduce the tubes into liquid nitrogen and transfer them to the lyophilizer overnight to remove water and methanol.
Place the tubes containing the organic phase in a fume hood and evaporate solvents under a gentle stream of nitrogen.
Store extracts at -80°C.
Place extract samples on ice and allow to thaw for 5 minutes.
Transfer 550 μL of NMR buffer (100 mM Na2HPO4, 0.1 mM TSP, pH 7.4 in 100% D2O) to each aqueous sample using a pipette.
Mix the buffer with the samples thoroughly.
Transfer the mixed samples into 5-mm NMR tubes on ice.
Dissolve organic extracts in 600 μL of deuterated chloroform (CHCl3-d1) containing 0.0027% tetramethylsilane (TMS) as an internal standard.
Vortex the dissolved samples to mix well.
Transfer the vortexed samples into 5-mm NMR tubes and seal them.
Store the organic phase samples up to 12 hours at 4°C.
Introduce the sample into the NMR spectrometer.
Set the temperature to 27°C for aqueous samples or 25°C for organic samples and allow to stabilize for 5 minutes.
Record 1H 1D NOESY NMR spectra with 400 scans for aqueous extracts.
Apply settings of 64k data points digitalized over a spectral width of 30 ppm, a 4-s relaxation delay between FIDs, and a water presaturation pulse of 25 Hz.
Record 1H 1D NOESY NMR spectra with 128 scans for organic extracts.
Apply settings of 64k data points digitalized over a spectral width of 30 ppm and a 4-s relaxation delay between FIDs.
Acquire 2D experiments for selected representative samples to confirm metabolite assignment.
Perform total correlation spectroscopy (TOCSY) on the aqueous phase and organic phase with 256–512 t1 increments and collect 32–96 transients.
Set the relaxation delays to 1.5 seconds and acquire experiments in phase-sensitive mode.
Record TOCSY spectra using a standard MLEV-17 pulse sequence with mixing times of 65 ms.
Perform Fourier transformation on each spectrum.
Multiply the FID values by an exponential function with a 0.5-Hz line broadening factor.
Perform automatic phase correction on each spectrum.
Adjust manually if phase is not correct after automatic correction.
Reference the spectra of the aqueous extracts to the TSP peak (0.00 ppm).
Reference the spectra of the organic phase to the TMS peak (0 ppm) using Mnova 12 or ChenomX.
Assign signals to metabolite identities by comparison to reference values for chemical shift and multiplicity.
Generate automatic integration regions in Mnova 12 or ChenomX, taking into account signal assignment.
Generate integration tables in Mnova 12 or ChenomX by applying automatic integration with the GSD deconvolution option.
Normalize integration tables to total intensity.
Extract the total mRNA from five Drosophila larvae using an RNeasy Mini Kit (Qiagen Cat#74106).
Treat RNA with an RNase-Free DNase Set (Qiagen Cat#79254) to remove contaminating DNA.
Synthesize cDNA using the SuperScript III First-Strand Synthesis System for RT-PCR with random oligo-dT primers.
Perform quantitative real-time PCR using SYBR Green PCR Master Mix and gene-specific primers on an ABI 7500 system.
Normalize the expression to β-actin.
Rinse 15 larvae (three replicates per sample) in PBS and dry on tissue paper.
Immerse each larva individually in Schneider’s Drosophila medium.
Carefully tear the cuticles to release the hemolymph.
Puncture a cross using a #22 surgical blade and collect larvae in a 0.5 mL tube.
Place the 0.5 mL tube with a punctured hole inside a 1.5 mL tube.
Spin using a 5415 R centrifuge three times for 3 seconds each at room temperature with caps open.
Transfer 10 μL of the supernatant to a new 1.5 mL tube.
Keep samples on ice before and after larval cuticle breakage to prevent melanization.
Measure glucose levels using an appropriate assay kit.
Measure trehalose levels using an appropriate assay kit.
Determine cholesterol levels using an Amplex Red Cholesterol Assay Kit (ThermoFisher Scientific Cat#A12216).
Analyze triglyceride levels using a Serum Triglyceride Determination Kit (Sigma-Aldrich Cat#TR0100-1KT).
Use GAHK20 Glucose Assay Kit for measuring glucose levels in dissected tissues or whole larvae according to manufacturer's instructions.
Convert trehalose to glucose using porcine trehalase, incubating all standards and samples at 37°C for 18-24 hours, then measure glucose using the GAHK20 kit.
Break down glycogen into free glucose using amyloglucosidase and quantify using GAHK20 assay.
Collect 10–20 larvae at the stage of interest using forceps.
Place larvae in a petri dish layered with Sylgard 184 transparent resin containing drops of cold 1× PBS.
Remove brain lobes by holding the larval body with one pair of forceps and pulling from the larval mouth hook with a second pair.
Remove fat bodies by holding the larval body with one pair of forceps and pulling from the larval mouth hook with a second pair.
Discard the larval body after dissection.
Remove excess unwanted tissue with fine mounted pins.
Place clean fly tissues in a glass well containing 150 μL of cold 1× PBS.
Add 50 μL of 16% paraformaldehyde for a final concentration of 4% paraformaldehyde.
Incubate the tissue on an orbital shaker with gentle agitation for 20 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Wash fixed tissues three times with 1× PBS.
Add 200 μL of blocking solution (5% normal goat serum) and incubate the tissues on an orbital shaker with gentle agitation for at least 30 minutes at room temperature in the dark.
Dilute primary antibodies (mouse anti-Dlg 4F3 or rat anti-DE-Cad DCAD2) in 0.3% Triton in 1× PBS.
Incubate larval tissues with diluted primary antibodies on an orbital shaker overnight (10–12 h) at room temperature in the dark.
If the ambient temperature is very high, use a humidified chamber to avoid evaporation and add moist papers to the chamber.
Wash the samples three times with PBS.
Dilute secondary antibodies in 0.3% Triton in 1× PBS.
Incubate with secondary antibodies in the dark for 3 h at room temperature.
Wash the samples three times with PBS.
Rinse larval tissues three times with PBS after incubation with secondary antibodies.
Incubate larval tissues for 40 min with a 1:500 dilution of PBS containing 1 mg/ml Nile Red.
Add 4 μL of Vectashield mounting medium with DAPI.
Mount larval tissues using the bridge method to preserve their three-dimensional configuration.
Use a Zeiss LSM 880 confocal microscope with Airyscan for super-resolution imaging of larval brains, fat bodies, and prothoracic gland cells.
Measure total fluorescence intensity or lipid droplet size in larval tissues using ImageJ software.
